nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every set partition $P$ of $\{-n, \dots, n\}$, every Adler block label $p$ of $P$ is an integer with $1 \le p \le n$.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $P$ a set partition of the integer interval $\{-n, \dots, n\}$; for $x$ in this interval write $P(x)$ for the block of $P$ containing $x$. The Adler block labels of $P$ are the integers $p$ with $1 \le p \le n$ such that $p \le q$ for every positive $q \in P(p)$ and $p < -q$ for every negative $q \in P(p)$; that is, $p$ is the least positive element of its block and is smaller than…

nodes.summary: For every natural number $s$, the doubled word of the singleton $\{s\}$ is $f(\{s\}) = s\,s$, the word of length two whose letters are both $s$.
nodes.title: The doubled word of a singleton

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\}$ of natural numbers, the doubled word of $S$ is $f(S) = s_1 s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k$, which lists the elements of $S$ in increasing order with each one written twice; $f(\emptyset)$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Doubled word

These are the flattened partitions of length $n$ of Nabawanda,…

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $|\mathrm{flat}(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$: words $w_1 w_2 \cdots w_{2n}$ of natural numbers that are Stirling permutations of order $n$ and whose runs (maximal contiguous weakly increasing subwords) have weakly increasing leading letters, read from left to right.
nodes.title: Number of flattened Stirling permutations

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, exactly one flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has exactly one run.
nodes.title: Exactly one flattened Stirling permutation has one run

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the number $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_{n+1})|$ of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n + 1$ with exactly two runs equals $3(2^n - 1) - 2n$.
nodes.title: Closed form for flattened Stirling permutations with two runs

nodes.summary: Write $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_n)|$ for the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$ with exactly two runs. Then $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_1)| = 0$, and for every natural number $n \ge 1$, $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_{n+1})| = 2\,|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_n)| + 2n - 1$.
nodes.title: Recursion for flattened Stirling permutations with two runs

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $|\mathrm{flat}_k(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$ with exactly $k$ runs, where a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword.
nodes.title: Counting flattened Stirling permutations by runs

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$ let $D_n$ be the $n$-th Dowling number of the group of order $2$, that is, the $(q, r)$-Dowling number $D_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ built from the $(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second kind with $m = 2$, $r = 1$, $q = 1$. Then for every complex number $x$ the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} D_n x^n / n!$ is summable with sum $\exp\bigl(x + (e^{2x} - 1)/2\bigr)$.
nodes.title: Exponential generating function of the Dowling numbers

nodes.summary: The word $w = 1\,1\,2\,2\,9\,9\,3\,8\,8\,3\,4\,6\,6\,7\,7\,4\,5\,5$ of length $18$ is flattened (the leading letters of its runs, read left to right, are weakly increasing), and it has exactly $4$ runs, where a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword.
nodes.title: A flattened word with four runs

nodes.summary: A word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of natural numbers is flattened when the leading letters of its runs, read left to right, are weakly increasing. Here a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword, so position $i$ starts a run when $i = 1$ or $w_{i-1} > w_i$; the condition is that $w_i \le w_j$ whenever $i < j$ and both positions start runs.
nodes.title: Flattened words

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, some flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has exactly $\lceil 2n/3 \rceil$ runs, and no flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has more.
nodes.title: Maximum number of runs of a flattened Stirling permutation

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the partition of the integer interval $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$ into a single block is a type $B$ set partition: its only block is closed under negation, so it is the unique block equal to its own negative (the zero-block).
nodes.title: The one-block partition is of type B

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a set partition $P$ of the integer interval $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$ is of type $B$ if for every block $\beta$ of $P$ the set $-\beta = \{-x : x \in \beta\}$ is again a block of $P$, and exactly one block $\beta$ of $P$ satisfies $-\beta = \beta$.
nodes.title: Type $B$ set partitions

nodes.summary: For every finite set $S$ of natural numbers with elements $s_1 < \dots < s_k$, the doubled word $f(S) = s_1 s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k$ has length $2|S|$.
nodes.title: Length of the doubled word

nodes.summary: For every finite set $S$ of natural numbers with elements $s_1 < \dots < s_k$, the wrapped word $g(S) = s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k s_1$ (the empty word when $S = \emptyset$) has length $2|S|$.
nodes.title: Length of the wrapped word

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the set of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n + 1$ is in bijection with the set of type $B$ set partitions of $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$.
nodes.title: Flattened Stirling permutations and type $B$ set partitions

Let $P_0$ be the set of nonnegative elements of the…

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every type $B$ set partition $P$ of $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$, the word $\varphi(P) = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_{2(n+1)}$ of $P$ is a Stirling permutation of order $n + 1$ and is flattened.
nodes.title: The word of a type $B$ set partition is a flattened Stirling permutation

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a set partition $P$ of $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$, let $L(P)$ be the list of $P$: the list of natural numbers built from the blocks of $P$ (via the shift map and the doubled and wrapped words). The word $\varphi(P) = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_{2(n+1)}$ has $w_i$ equal to the $i$-th entry of $L(P)$ when $L(P)$ has at least $i$ entries, and $w_i = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The word of a set partition of $(-n, n)$

nodes.summary: For the map $h(S) = \{|i| + 1 : i \in S\}$ on finite sets of integers, $h(\{-2, 0, 1\}) = \{1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: An example of the shift map

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of integers, $h(S) = \{|i| + 1 : i \in S\}$, a finite set of natural numbers.
nodes.title: The shift map

Write $P_0$ for the set of nonnegative elements of the block of $\pi$ containing $0$. Let $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_m$ be the blocks kept by Adler's labelling, exactly one from each pair $\{\beta, -\beta\}$ of distinct blocks, namely the block containing the…
nodes.title: Number of runs of the word of a type $B$ set partition

nodes.summary: A run of a word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ of natural numbers is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword. The number of runs of $w$ is the number of positions $i < m$ that start a run, that is, with $i = 0$ or $w_{i-1} > w_i$; the empty word has no runs.
nodes.title: Number of runs of a word

nodes.summary: Position $i$ of a word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ of natural numbers starts a run when $i = 0$ or the letter before it is larger, that is, $w_{i-1} > w_i$. Runs are the maximal contiguous weakly increasing subwords, so these are exactly the positions where a run begins.
nodes.title: Start of a run

nodes.summary: The wrapped word $g(\emptyset)$ of the empty set is the empty word.
nodes.title: Wrapped word of the empty set

nodes.summary: For every natural number $s$, the wrapped word of the singleton $\{s\}$ is $g(\{s\}) = s\,s$, the word of length two both of whose letters are $s$.
nodes.title: Wrapped word of a singleton

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\}$ of natural numbers, the wrapped word $g(S)$ is $s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k s_1$: the smallest element, then each larger element written twice in increasing order, then the smallest element again. For $S = \emptyset$, $g(S)$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Wrapped word of a finite set
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
